uncited: What sets this family apart from siblings like [Time-dependent NeRF with Continuous Camera Motion](12399-time-dependent-nerf-with-continuous-camera-motion.md) is the explicit optimization of discrete camera poses per image rather than continuous motion functions, and from [Camera Preconditioning](12545-camera-preconditioning.md) by focusing on the joint gradient-based update of poses and scene geometry rather than preconditioning the optimizer for faster convergence.

All methods in this family share the core mechanism of differentiable rendering, where the rendered pixel color $\hat{C}(r)$ is a differentiable function of the camera pose $P$ and the NeRF parameters $\Theta$.
where $C(r)$ is the ground-truth pixel color.
The gradient $\nabla_P \mathcal{L}$ allows the camera pose to be updated via an optimizer (e.g., Adam, SGD) in lockstep with the NeRF weights.
**Ray Casting:** Computing ray origins $\hat{o}$ and directions $\hat{d}$ from pixel coordinates using current camera estimates.

Subsequent work expanded this to include depth priors ([NoPe-NeRF](8705-nope-nerf.md), [AltNeRF](8763-altnerf.md)) and specific applications like medical imaging ([Hybrid 2D/3D Registration](8120-hybrid-2d-3d-registration-optimization-pipeline.md)) and robotics ([Vision-Only Pose Filtering](10501-vision-only-pose-filtering-in-a-nerf.md), [Online Receding Horizon Replanning](10509-online-receding-horizon-replanning.md), [NeRF-based Trajectory Optimization](10632-nerf-based-trajectory-optimization.md)).
The technique of NeRF registration using Viewshed Fields was introduced in [VF-NeRF](S1).
